A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SEPAL/BLOCS research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reformatting and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original downstream prediction, link prediction, scalability, and ablation results in Section 5 and Appendices C–F.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, prior-benchmark evaluations, a core-selection analysis, and a continual-learning experiment.

M1.justification: The original core training, BLOCS decomposition, and propagation rules remain intact. Section G.3 introduces SEPAL-CL, which initializes an updated graph from previously computed embeddings and performs five propagation steps to update existing entities and embed new ones.

E1.justification: Section C.5 adds downstream attribute-prediction tasks on FB15k-237, YAGO3-10, and Wikidata5M. Section G.3 adds YAGO3-2022 and a temporal graph-update scenario using the 2014 and 2022 releases. The original large-graph and downstream-table coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated Freebase comparisons with SMORE and GraSH (Table 7), previously only discussed, and a Mini YAGO3 comparison with DistMult-ERAvg (Table 12). Table 8 additionally compares SEPAL with published KE-GCN results and MTT/STD variants of KGE baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include 128-dimensional embeddings and the prior benchmark's evaluation script with weighted F1 and regression RSE, specified single-GPU training budgets for SMORE and GraSH, and temporal embedding reuse versus training from scratch. These expand evaluation design; the original splits and hyperparameter grids are retained.

E4.justification: Table 11 adds a controlled degree-versus-PageRank core-selection analysis with other hyperparameters fixed. Section G.3 adds a case study of update cost and retained predictive quality against retraining. The existing BLOCS, METIS, propagation, and hyperparameter analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five repeats of five-fold cross-validation, critical-difference significance analyses, and the 95% regression confidence interval in Figure 9. The new tables introduce no new repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing figure results and link-prediction Table 6 are retained, while several new studies add performance and runtime entries. Table 8 reports FB15k-237 weighted F1 of 0.853 for SEPAL versus 0.890 for RotatE (MTT). Table 15 reports SEPAL-CL scoring 0.962 in 1m 08s versus 0.988 in 1h 05m 07s for SEPAL trained from scratch. These are new comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 adds explicit SGNS and binary cross-entropy loss definitions and their special-case relationship. SEPAL's alignment energy, queriability definition, and Appendix D derivations and proof are retained. The convergence statement added to the main text already appeared in v1's Appendix D.2.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that SEPAL improves downstream features through core-based propagation and achieves large-graph scalability through BLOCS, including embedding WikiKG90Mv2 on one 32GB V100. The reorganized contribution list and additional appendix evidence preserve these central claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for weaker performance on tiny graphs, budget-dependent SMORE results, and graph-dependent PageRank benefits. Continual-learning applicability is qualified by unchanged relation types. Section 4 also presents alignment leading to queriability more cautiously as an argument.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code link and documents configurations, evaluation scripts, and training budgets for the new experiments. Section 3.1 newly specifies handling disconnected inputs by adding smaller components to the core; this disclosure does not establish a change to the earlier implementation or retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted references on complex querying and out-of-sample embeddings, including Albooyeh et al. (2020), and explains SEPAL's distinction from DistMult-ERAvg. The introduction also acknowledges single-machine memory-hierarchy approaches alongside distributed systems. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten into labeled motivation paragraphs and four explicit contributions. The BLOCS overview moves from Appendix E.2 into Section 3.1. Expanded background explanations, revised subsection organization, and the added NeurIPS checklist substantially change document organization while retaining much of the original prose.

P2.justification: v2 adopts NeurIPS typography and title/header formatting, changes caption presentation, and reflows displays throughout the document. It adds six tables covering comparisons, core selection, and continual learning. All 23 original figure graphics are retained unchanged, although their placement changes.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens comparative validation through additional scalable systems and a closely related propagation baseline, and tests a prior published benchmark that exposes a small-graph limitation. It also turns the continual-learning conjecture into a documented experiment and adds code-access information. These address important validation and applicability gaps in v1. Training-budget dependence and the unchanged-relations assumption still limit the new findings; the theoretical proof and uncertainty reporting remain largely unchanged.
